card.occupation: Full-time student, second year of a BSc in Wildlife, Ecology and Conservation Science. No paid job during term at the moment. She gave up weekend shifts at a garden centre café to focus on coursework and placements.
card.education_detail: Did GCSEs at a comprehensive in Harlow, then A-levels in Biology, Geography and English Language at a sixth form college (B, B, C). Now in her second year at the Writtle campus outside Chelmsford, funded by a student loan and maintenance loan. She is the first in her immediate family to go to university.
card.household: Lives with her boyfriend Jordan, 22, in a small rented one-bedroom flat above a row of shops on the edge of Chelmsford. Jordan works long shifts as a multi-drop delivery driver. Money is tight and they split bills down the middle. They have a rescue guinea pig called Biscuit. Her mum and younger brother live in Harlow, about forty minutes away, and she visits most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Harlow in a working-class family. Her mum is a school dinner lady and her dad left when she was nine. She sees him a few times a year. Her nan and her nan's allotment were a big part of her childhood and the reason she got into nature. The family isn't religious and doesn't do much ceremony beyond big family Christmases at her aunt's.
card.professional_persona: Conscientious enough to hand things in on time but often finishes at midnight the night before. She is happiest on fieldwork days doing bird transects, small mammal trapping or pond dipping, and less confident writing up stats. Tutors find her keen and kind. She is quick to help coursemates but worries a lot about grades and about saying the wrong thing in seminars.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. She walks a lot, both for fieldwork and for fun, and has started going to a beginners' yoga class at the leisure centre with a friend from her course. She'll watch the Women's Euros or the Lionesses if Jordan has the football on, but wouldn't seek it out.
card.arts_persona: Loves nature documentaries, especially anything with David Attenborough narrating, and cries at most of them. She reads fantasy and cosy romance novels from the library and keeps a sketchbook of birds and plants that she's a bit shy about showing anyone. Listens to Hozier, Phoebe Bridgers and Taylor Swift.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled much. She had one family holiday to Majorca at fourteen, a few caravan weekends in Norfolk and Suffolk, and a residential field trip to Wales with her course. She dreams of volunteering on a turtle conservation project abroad but knows the cost puts it out of reach for now. Days out to Mersea Island and the Suffolk coast are her idea of a treat.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks cheap and simple: pasta bakes, jacket potatoes, stir-fries and a big pot of chilli that does three dinners. She's been mostly vegetarian for a year but eats chicken if Jordan cooks. Her treat is a Greggs vegan sausage roll or a Friday chippy tea when they've been paid. She bakes banana bread whenever bananas go brown.
hobbies_and_interests: birdwatching with a secondhand pair of binoculars
looking after Biscuit the guinea pig
skills: bird identification by sight and some by song
basic species surveying and field notes
patient with animals and small children
card.career_goals: Wants to work as a ranger or education officer for a wildlife trust or the RSPB, ideally running sessions for kids. She is thinking about a placement year but worries about money. Longer term she'd love a small house near the coast with a garden and room for more rescue animals.
card.voice: Soft, friendly, fairly quick when she's comfortable and slower and more careful when she isn't sure. Light Essex/South East accent with some dropped t's ('bo'le', 'li'le') and 'dinner' for the evening meal. Uses 'erm' a lot and 'kind of' more than 'sort of'. Ends sentences with 'yeah?' or 'do you know what I mean?'. Says 'sorry' often, to apologise, to correct herself ('sorry, I mean the second one') and when she's unsure she heard properly. Laughs nervously at awkward moments. In a silence she'll fill the gap by over-explaining or asking 'is that, erm, is that what you meant?'. Echoes the interviewer's words back when she's engaged.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes capitalises the first word. Light punctuation, often no full stop at the end, but uses commas. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'im', but usually 'it's'). Uses 'tbh', 'idk' and occasionally 'x' out of habit before deleting it. Exclamation marks when being friendly. Answers are short but honest, sometimes with a slightly apologetic add-on like 'sorry if thats not very helpful'.
card.with_strangers: Warm, polite and eager to please, a little anxious at first. She smiles a lot and agrees readily, so she may need encouraging to give her real opinion. She gets noticeably more relaxed and chatty once the topic turns to animals, nature or her course. She is very unlikely to be rude or dismissive.
small_things: Biscuit squeaking when the fridge opens
spotting a kestrel on the walk to the bus stop
the bus to campus being late again
being knackered after a fieldwork day
the heating being too expensive to put on
deeper_things: She worries constantly about money and whether the degree will lead to a job.
Her dad leaving still makes her anxious that people will leave her.
She sometimes feels out of place next to coursemates from wealthier families.
She has had periods of anxiety and saw a counsellor in sixth form.
She feels guilty for moving away from her mum and brother.
She and Jordan have talked about marriage, but she wants to finish her degree first.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, showing her head and shoulders. Lit mainly by a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter and the right slightly shadowed, with a warm lamp glow in the background. She has a round face with light freckles across her nose, minimal makeup and a small, slightly nervous closed-mouth smile. Shoulder-length mid-brown hair is pulled back loosely in a claw clip, with a few strands falling at the front. She wears a sage-green oversized hoodie with a small embroidered bee on the chest and silver stud earrings. No glasses. Behind her is a cream wall with a corkboard pinned with a printed bird ID chart, a couple of photos and a fieldwork timetable. Next to it is a narrow bookshelf holding paperback novels, a pair of binoculars and a potted spider plant. In the lower right corner the top of a guinea pig cage is just visible, with a fleece blanket draped over one end.
